notes: An explicit corporate or membership-body suffix. "Rural Health Medical Program Inc." is a real Alabama FQHC that the §6.1 `program` pattern would otherwise send to UNASSIGNED.

A named academic institution. Ten Nevada residency and fellowship awards name "University of Nevada, Reno <specialty> Residency Program" - real recipients that the `program` and `expansion` patterns both catch.
A named provider organisation. "Dignity Health Dominican Hospital ... Expansion Program" is a real recipient.
A named foundation. Several states administer RHTP through one (VHHA Foundation, Foundation for Healthy Communities) and they are genuine Tier 3 recipients with an intermediary role.

An explicit statement that the recipient is NOT resolved. Beats the entity override in both directions: "16 Strategically Located Rural Hospitals (unnamed, subrecipient group)" contains `hospitals` and is still not a named recipient, and "Various Rural Health Clinics" contains `clinic`.

A provider organisation whose name carries no corporate suffix. Spec 0.3a names Beebe Healthcare, TidalHealth and Nemours Children's Health as the worked examples of hospitals that were coded away; without this marker each fails the entity test and a 6.2 split that would have surfaced them is rejected. Deliberately does NOT match a bare 'Health', so 'Oregon Health' in 'Oregon Health & Science University' still fails and the & is not read as a delimiter.

A children's hospital or system. A large class of them -- Nemours Children's Health, Children's Healthcare of Atlanta, Children's Health Dallas -- carries no corporate suffix and no 'hospital' token, and spec 0.3a names Nemours as one of the Delaware records coded away. Kept separate from the bare 'health' case, which stays unmatched on purpose.
